verdict.rationale: Sumsub documents its own AML Screening product, which screens against sanctions, PEP, watchlists and adverse media, with configurable lists and fuzziness. It also documents verification levels, a single REST API for applicant processing, and a dashboard applicant profile for manual approve/reject. However, the evidence never explicitly states that AML screening runs inside the same verification level or that hits are reviewed on the same applicant surface. missing for 10: explicit documentation that AML screening is a step within the verification level/flow, evidence that watchlist hits appear and are resolved in the same applicant review surface, API-level evidence of screening results, independent/hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an ops lead, I can screen verified users against sanctions, PEP, and adverse-media watchlists as part of the same verification — one vendor, one API, one review surface

citations.quote: screening against constantly changing sanctions lists, PEP lists and data, watchlists, and adverse media
Configure your AML screening settings to suit your needs by screening against targeted lists and categories that are relevant to your business, and adjust fuzziness levels to suit.
A level is a sequence of steps that your applicants have to take to verify their identity.
With the Sumsub API, you can process the applicant data and documents submitted for verification through simple RESTful APIs.
You can approve or reject an applicant regardless of their status
